changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/console-form-container-specs-one-declaration-5596.md`

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#5542 converged the LEAF of this contract — the field spec — and left the two containers above it untouched, because converging them was a bigger call than a mechanical import. `FormSectionSpec` and `FormViewSpec` were each hand-declared twice under the same names, once in `packages/app-shell`'s `SchemaForm.tsx` and once in `apps/console`'s `FormPage.tsx`. Unlike the leaf — whose console copy was a clean subset — these two had **already drifted, in both directions**, so neither copy was a subset of the other and there were two live answers to "what may an author write":

### `.changeset/console-form-field-spec-one-declaration-5542.md`

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#5040 was not a missing key. It was that **two hand-written descriptions of one contract drifted**, and nothing could notice, because each was only ever checked against itself. PR #5537 converged the two app-shell descriptions into `views/metadata-admin/form-spec.ts`. A **third** survived in `apps/console`: `FormPage.tsx` declared its own nine-key `interface FormFieldSpec`, under the same name, in a different package — so the same failure mode stayed fully available.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-runtime-default-seed-5727.md`

- names `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `readPrefill` in `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` seeded every declared default unconditionally. A `defaultValue` may be a literal, or an *instruction* the server resolves per insert — a `DEFAULT_VALUE_TOKENS` token (`NOW()`, `current_user`) or a CEL Expression envelope. Seeding one of those literally put the text `NOW()` into a datetime input on both `/forms/:name` and the public `/f/:slug` route, and submitting it sent that string as the field's value — which is neither absent nor null, so `ObjectQL.applyFieldDefaults` never resolved the declared default and the column stored the token text instead of a timestamp.

### `.changeset/console-formpage-visible-predicates-5594.md`

- names `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` is a **second, independent form renderer** — its own `buildSections`, its own JSX — and it serves both the public `/f/:slug` route and the internal `/forms/:name` route. It read neither spelling of the FormView field visibility predicate: a repo-wide grep for a `visibleWhen` / `visibleOn` *read* inside that file returned zero. So a field an author conditioned on `record.priority == 'urgent'` — legal, spec-strict metadata that `@objectstack/spec` normalises to `visibleWhen` (ADR-0089), and that the metadata-admin designer both authors and honours — rendered unconditionally on both routes. Fail-open and silent: the author saw the field always, with no diagnostic.

- names `FormPage.tsx` → `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` — edited by this change

  > objectui#2212 recorded this exact symptom and PR #2214 fixed it — in a **different chain**: `ModalForm` → `resolveFormViewLayout` → `@object-ui/plugin-form` `sectionFields.ts` → `@object-ui/components` `renderers/form/form.tsx`. `FormPage.tsx` is on that chain at no point, and #2212's regression pin lives with the chain it fixed, so nothing in the suite could see this copy. One contract, two implementations, each only ever checked against itself.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `fee1da595` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1440 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2022 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36113863516)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `735c9ed5724df24b64f855330b2951e59d536e92`

Reviewed against merge-base `0d5d66aee7ec565be12ae3bee218dc02e8af9531`; main at review time `fee1da5953bef4678168be546bffd46c67631fdf`. Diff: 3 files, +198 / -6 (`apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` +44/-6; new `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.widgetDegrade-10472.test.tsx` +135; new `.changeset/10472-formpage-widget-degrades-to-type.md` +19). Read via `git show refs/review/pr-10553:PATH`; the shared tree and the sibling worktrees were not checked out or edited. Zero GitHub writes.

### ① Derived judgments

**The binding text.** Installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (`dist/ui/index.js`, the `widget` describe on `FieldSchema`, with the tag-shaped placeholder spelled WIDGET here): "Form widget override — names a registered field component (resolved as `field:WIDGET`) to render this field instead of the `type` default. Degrades to the `type` renderer when unregistered." Its JSDoc adds "Unknown/unregistered values fall back to the `type` renderer, so it degrades safely" and names `form.tsx` as the honouring consumer. Card: "The shape of the fix: an unregistered `widget` falls through to the `type` leg of the same resolver. ⛔ Not a local list of known widgets." Triage (5828139551): "an unregistered `widget` falls through to the `type` leg of the same resolver; ⛔ not a local list of known widgets. Measure the record form (`form.tsx`) in the same round."

1. **Guard flip — `FormPage.tsx:685-687` (head).** Merge-base `:649` was `if (field.widget) return resolveFormWidgetType(field.widget);`. Head reads `if (field.widget && namesRegisteredWidget(field.widget)) { return resolveFormWidgetType(field.widget); }`, and on a false predicate control reaches the arity leg (`:688-693`) and the type leg (`:694`) of the same function. RIGHT: this is literally the card's "falls through to the `type` leg of the same resolver".

2. **The predicate — `FormPage.tsx:652-654`, sentinel `UNKNOWN_SPELLING_WIDGET = 'text'` at `:630`.** `resolveFormWidgetType(widget) !== 'text' || widget === 'text'`. Traced against the resolver at `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:3896-3905` (head): it answers (a) the spelling itself when it is a `fieldWidgetMap` key, (b) the spelling itself when `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` holds it, (c) the `field:`-stripped alias target when that is a map key, else (d) the literal `'text'`. So `'text'` comes back only from `widget === 'text'` (case a, kept by the second disjunct), from an alias whose target is `text` (none exist: the table at `packages/fields/src/field-type-alias.ts:104-200` maps only `text` to `field:text`, and every other target — `password`, `slider`, `boolean`, `lookup`, `file`, `code`, `object`, `grid`, `auto_number`, and the rest — is present in the `fieldWidgetMap` key set I listed from `index.tsx:3785-3862`), or from the unknown tail (d). The predicate is therefore exactly "the shared resolver knows this spelling", with no widget list: RIGHT against the card's ⛔. Coupling note, not a defect: the sentinel restates the resolver's documented fallback string; should a future alias ever target `field:text`, that alias would degrade to type here, which the describe ("names a registered field component") still permits.

3. **Retired spelling.** `widget: 'owner'`: resolver case (b) answers `'owner'`, predicate true, key `'owner'`, and `getLazyFieldWidget` returns `RetiredFieldTombstone` (`index.tsx:3936`). RIGHT: the tombstone is preserved, and control pin 2 (below) proves it. The `field:`-qualified spellings take a different path: `isRetiredFieldType` (`packages/core/src/utils/retired-field-types.ts`, `hasOwnProperty` on the exact spelling) strips no prefix, and `mapFieldTypeToFormType('field:owner')` misses the type map and the retired gate and returns `field:text`, so the resolver answers `'text'`, the predicate is false, and the row degrades to its `type`. After the PR `widget: 'field:owner'` on a `user` row mounts the user picker (before: a text input) and `widget: 'field:textarea'` on a `textarea` row mounts the textarea (before: a text input). Neither refused before, neither refuses after: no guard existed on this seam to weaken. Consistent with the describe; the tombstone prescription's sentence "The `widget: 'field:owner'` spelling is retired with it" was never honoured by this resolver chain, which is a pre-existing gap the PR body records under H4 and not this card's ask.

4. **Docblock edits — `FormPage.tsx:107-113` (header) and `:656-679` (resolver steps).** The prose now says an authored `widget` wins "when it names a registered widget" and otherwise degrades to the `type` renderer per `FieldSchema.widget`. TRUE against `:685-694`. The `namesRegisteredWidget` docblock (`:632-651`) says a spelling answered with `text` that the author did not write as `text` "named nothing", and that a registered key, a retired spelling and an alias of a registered key keep resolving: TRUE by item 2. Its opening question "name a widget the shared registry holds" is loose for the retired case (the map holds no `owner`; the docblock itself carves out the tombstone) — style, not a defect.

5. **Both callers agree.** `rowLabelProps` (`:1686`) and `FieldInput` (`:1805`) call the same `resolveFieldWidgetKey`, so label association and the mounted widget cannot name different widgets after the flip. The widget leg now evaluates the resolver twice on a hit (predicate, then return); both calls are pure except the once-per-spelling retired reporter, which case (b) short-circuits before `mapFieldTypeToFormType`, so nothing is reported twice.

6. **Nothing done that was not asked.** Three files, all inside the surface the card names; no list of widgets; no change to `packages/fields`, `packages/core`, `form.tsx`, or any barrel.

7. **Nothing asked is missing.** The card's fix shape is met (items 1-2). The triage's "Measure the record form (`form.tsx`) in the same round" is answered in the PR body (same symptom, not changed) and is consistent with source: `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx:354` (`f?.widget || f?.field?.widget || f?.type`), `:1914` (`(f as any).widget || f.type`), `:2726` (`widget || fieldProps.field?.widget || type`), and the unregistered branch's own spelling table at `:3522-3525` (`secret` and `ui:password` answer `password`, the objectui#5322 / objectui#5375 rulings). So the record form still breaches the same describe, and the spec JSDoc names it as the consumer; that is a real remaining breach that needs its own card, not a defect of this PR, whose card scopes the site to `resolveFieldWidgetKey`.

8. **Existing pins edited or deleted: none.** No existing test file is in the diff. The sibling pins that read the widget leg survive by construction: `FormPage.sharedFieldResolver-10179.test.tsx:170-175` (`widget: 'text'` on a select answers `text`) is kept by the `widget === 'text'` disjunct; `:153-166` (`object-ref`, `filter-condition`, `recipient-picker`) are map keys; `:178-183` (view beats object) reads precedence, not the predicate. No guard weakened.

9. **New pins can fail.** `FormPage.widgetDegrade-10472.test.tsx`, real widgets (no `getLazyFieldWidget` stub), the same fetch-stub shape as `FormPage.retiredFieldType-10176.test.tsx:88-125`, the same `sonner` mock as `FormPage.sharedWidgets-10179.test.tsx:44`, beside the existing FormPage tests as required.
   - Pin 1 (`:95-99`, object field) and pin 2 (`:101-108`, form-view field), the card's two reproductions: positive leg `findByRole('combobox', { name: 'Stage' })`, negative leg `queryByRole('textbox', { name: 'Stage' })` is null. At merge-base the row mounts `TextField` (a textbox) and no combobox, so the positive leg goes red. The combobox is reachable by label because `select` is labelled `'control'` (`FIELD_WIDGET_LABELLING`) and `SelectTrigger` spreads the DOM id (`SelectField.tsx:184,200`).
   - Control 1 (`:110-115`): `widget: 'radio'` on the same select expects a radiogroup and no combobox and no textbox. A change that ignored `widget`, or a predicate that always answers false, mounts the select instead: red. Lit.
   - Control 2 (`:117-134`): `widget: 'owner'` on a `user` row expects the tombstone and zero `input, button, [role="combobox"]` inside the row. A predicate answering false mounts `UserField` (a lookup trigger button): red. Lit, and it carries its own negative leg.
   - Not executed by this seat (read-only review); the run is CI's, see ③.

10. **Pre-existing, not introduced:** `resolveFormWidgetType` indexes `fieldWidgetLoaderByKey` by plain property read (`index.tsx:3897`), so `widget: 'constructor'` resolved to itself before the PR and still does. Out of scope.

### ② Semver level
